hook: Sampling a classical piece in a pop song is not 'ruining' it, it's literally what classical composers did to each other for 300 years.
script: Sampling a classical piece in a pop song is not 'ruining' it — it's literally what classical composers did to each other for 300 years. Beethoven borrowed themes. Brahms borrowed themes. An entire tradition of 'variations on a theme by so-and-so' exists because composers constantly remixed each other's material, and nobody called it disrespectful — it was a tribute. So when a pop song samples an aria or an orchestral hook, that's not modern disrespect toward 'real music.' That's the exact same tradition classical music was already running on.

hook: A Black composer's opera didn't play at the Met until 2021. Let that sit for a second.
script: A Black composer's opera didn't play at the Met until 2021. Let that sit for a second. Terence Blanchard's Fire Shut Up in My Bones opened the Met's season in September 2021 — the first opera by a Black composer in the company's 138-year history. Not the first great one. The first one, period, in a 138-year-old institution. I'm not telling you this to be discouraging. I'm telling you because knowing exactly how recent that is changes how you think about what 'tradition' in this art form actually means, and who it was built to include.

Gaynor Minden introduced additional skin-tone shades in 2017. Freed of London followed in 2018. Most other major brands didn't add options until 2020, after major public pressure. For basically the entire modern history of ballet, 'pointe shoe pink' meant one specific pale shade, and every dancer who didn't match it had to paint or dye their own shoes just to look 'finished' on stage. That's not ancient history. Some of the dancers who dealt with that are still performing right now.
